ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: A RimWorld of Magic
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Mage and fighter classes, a Magic research tab, enchanting, golems and magical threats
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A mage who runs out of mana has to wait for it to refill, so keep archers on the wall beside them.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: A RimWorld of Magic gives some colonists a class. Mages spend mana on spells, fighters spend stamina on combat techniques, and every class levels up its own ability tree. The mod also adds enchanting, golems, portals and new magical dangers, and enemy classes use their powers against you. Its research lives in a separate Magic tab, and almost every project there is neolithic or medieval tier (only the mecha golem projects are industrial), so it suits a medieval game.

li.heading: Classes
li.text: Classes are traits. The mod lists over 35 of them, from fire, ice and lightning mages to druids, priests, necromancers, paladins, rangers, gladiators and monks. Some colonists have the talent for a class but no class yet, and an item teaches them one:

table.li: Trait | Can become | Taught by
Magically gifted | A mage | An arcane tome, such as Arcane Tome: Fire
Physically adept | A fighter | A combat manual, such as Combat Style: Ranger

li.after: Check every newcomer's traits for these two, and keep any tome or manual you find for them. Psycasts from Vanilla Psycasts Expanded run on their own, so a colony can have both mages and psycasters.

li.heading: Magicyte and enchanting
li.text:
Raw magicyte turns up while mining any rock: every strike has a small chance, but deep drilling never finds it. It is cut into enchanting gems at the gemcrafting table. Mining by hand is the only steady source of magicyte for enchanting, so keep someone at it.
Only a mage can enchant. Enchantments are permanent, one of each type per item, and do not raise the item's value.

li.heading: Magical threats
li.text: New threats include mana storms, elemental assaults, demon attacks, a wandering lich and enemy arcane raiding parties. In a raid, target enemy mages first, since one caster can do more damage than the rest of the raid.

points.li: Raised undead and spirits are not counted as people, so they make no wishes, keep no journals and form no friendships, and an enemy undead can't become a nemesis.
Healers such as priests and druids are favored for physician, and fighters for marshal. Mages like study hours, fighters like drills, and a mage may ask for a magic circle once you can build one.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Psycasts Expanded
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Psycasts rebuilt as a level-up tree with fifteen paths, from empath to conflagrator
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Meditation gives a psycaster experience, and each new level brings points to spend.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Vanilla Psycasts Expanded replaces Royalty's fixed list of psycasts with a role-playing system. A psycaster gains experience by meditating, levels up, and spends points on abilities in one or more paths or on their own psychic stats. Rarely, enemies send their own psycasters against you. It needs Royalty, and it can't be removed from a save.

li.heading: The fifteen paths
li.text: The paths are empath, skipmaster, conflagrator, protector, warlord, chronopath, archotechist, necropath, staticlord, archon, frostshaper, wildspeaker, harmonist, technomancer and nightstalker. Some are locked: archotechist needs an Imperial backstory, and wildspeaker needs a caster who can meditate on natural focus.

li.heading: Leveling up
li.text:
Meditation is how a psycaster levels up, so give each one a good meditation spot that suits their focus. There is no level cap, but you'll get more from leveling one or two paths deeply than from dabbling in many. Right-click an ability to let the psycaster cast it on their own.
Added to a running save, the mod turns existing psycasts into levels you can spend again. Caster gear research is medieval tier, but eltex gear is spacer tier, so a game held at medieval research won't reach it.

li.heading: Psycaster raids
li.text: Psycaster raids are a rare raid type for tribals and the Empire, and the game warns you when one is coming. When the warning letter names an enemy psycaster, make them your first target.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: An enemy psycaster who cuts someone down and escapes is remembered like any raider and can come back as a nemesis.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Elves (Continued)
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Wood, dark and high elves as xenotypes, with six factions, elven gear and two new beasts
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: An elf stops aging at thirty and keeps that face for the rest of a long life.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Elves (Continued) adds wood, dark and high elves as Biotech xenotypes, six medieval elven factions, three playable elven starts, elven weapons and armor, the ancient deer and the Cold One. These elves are long-lived humans: their ageless gene slows aging from age 13 and stops it entirely at 30. All three kinds are pretty, long-haired, beardless and point-eared, and dark elves are aggressive.

li.heading: The three houses

table.li: House | Faction you can deal with | Natural enemies | Player faction
Wood | Wood elves | Savage wood elves | Wood elf clan
Dark | Dark elves | Rough dark elves | Dark elf coven
High | High elves | Rough high elves | High elf colony

li.after: There is also a wood elf scenario to start from. Expect raids from the savage and rough elves; they carry bows and crossbows, so build cover along your walls. Before recruiting an elf, check their genes with Xenotype Summary's button.

li.heading: Elven gear
li.text: Three medieval research projects, one per house, unlock that house's weapons and armor: bows and greatbows, crossbows, swords, halberds, shields and named armor sets. Research your own house's equipment early; the gear is medieval and fits the rest of this modlist.

li.heading: Two new beasts
li.text: The ancient deer gives milk and wool. The Cold One is an egg-laying reptile that its description calls a dark elf mount.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The council reads biological age, which the ageless gene holds at about 30, so elves never count as old and stay able to set their heart on having a child.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Det's Xenotypes - Stoneborn
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Short, bearded, short-tempered master miners and builders, with their own dwarven clan
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Put a stoneborn in the mine and leave them to it; they're happiest underground.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: The Stoneborn are a Biotech xenotype of stout, bearded dwarves who live for mining, building and crafting. They are superb at all three, but slow, nearsighted, poor with people and quick to fight. The mod also adds a stoneborn clan faction made up entirely of dwarves, which is at war with every other faction but starts out neutral with you.

table.li: Genes | Effect
Aptitudes | Strong at mining and construction, remarkable at crafting; terrible at social work and poor with animals
Body | Slow, nearsighted, robust, psychically deaf and always bearded
Stonecall | A war cry that raises the caster's construction and mining speed by 30% for about 14 hours, usable once every 6 days
Undergrounder | Gives them the undergrounder trait, so they are happy indoors and under a mountain
Mighty liver | Immune to cirrhosis
Extended memory | Moods last 25% longer and skills fade more slowly
Long life | A 1.5 times longer lifespan
Irascible | Social fights are 1.5 times as likely

li.heading: Putting them to work
li.text:
Put stoneborn on mining, building and crafting, and keep them out of social jobs like warden and trader. Save the stonecall for a big push, such as finishing the walls before winter. Keep rivals apart, since an irascible stoneborn starts fights easily; the council's Bonds page shows who can't stand whom.
The Stoneborn Dwarven Style Pack and Stoneborn Delights in your list add dwarven furniture and food to go with them.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: As undergrounders they never ask the council for time outside, and they hate the harvest push decree. One with a passion for mining may set their heart on carving a home out of the mountain.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Goji's Fantasy Race: Merren
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Two merfolk xenotypes who need water, swim fast, sing and charm
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A merren far from water goes looking for rain or a river, and if she finds none she can die.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Merren are merfolk. Coastal merren are friendly swimmers and singers; abyssal merren are aggressive storm-callers with great psychic power. Both have fish tails and a hydration need, so they must reach rain or open water regularly. Its package id still carries the project's working name, Stagz Merfolk.

li.heading: Coastal and abyssal

table.li: Merren | Strengths | Weaknesses
Coastal | Swim fast; nimble, charming and good with animals | Terrible at mining and cooking
Abyssal | Call rain, see in the dark, extreme psychic sensitivity | Nearsighted, aggressive and very sensitive to sunlight

li.after: Keep abyssal merren out of the midday sun where you can.

li.heading: Keeping them watered
li.text:
Hydration refills in rain, marsh and rivers. Merren go looking for water on their own when it runs low, and at zero a merren dehydrates and can die. Settle them near a river or marsh, or in a rainy biome, and keep their work close to water.
With Dubs Bad Hygiene, baths can refill hydration too. That option is switched off by default; Dubs Bad Hygiene is in your list, so you can turn it on in the mod settings to let baths keep merren watered.

li.heading: Siren song and charm
li.text: Siren song overwhelms nearby enemies. Charm person compels a human or animal to join, but after 7 to 15 days a charmed person ends up staying loyal, leaving or turning aggressive, each equally likely. Charm people sparingly, and watch a charmed recruit closely for the first 15 days, since two times in three they leave or turn on you.

li.heading: Newcomers and extras
li.text: Merren may join through special events: one may rescue a colonist lying wounded on a shore, and with Royalty a merren virtuoso may answer a colonist's recital. The mod also brings a wood-fueled floating lantern, a squid dryad with Ideology, and waterborne plants with VE Plants More (in your list).

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Awakened Apes
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Five sapient ape xenotypes, from gentle gorillas to jittery monkeys
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The bonobo settled the quarrel in the kitchen before it came to blows.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Awakened Apes adds five playable ape xenotypes, each with its own strengths and temper. They speak broken English, so their social impact is halved, and they can only have children with their own species. It is a community update of an older monkey xenotype mod, and it needs Biotech.

li.heading: The five apes

points.li: Gorillas are strong, gentle haulers who are peaceful until provoked. Put them on hauling.
Chimpanzees are fast learners and deadly shots, with violent tendencies. Watch them around their rivals.
Bonobos are kind peacekeepers who settle quarrels through social bonding.
Orangutans are gifted artisans with psychic sensitivity who need little sleep. Put them on crafting.
Monkeys are small, anxious sharpshooters, good with plants and in a fight. Put them on the fields and the walls.

li.after: Use apes as specialists like this, and keep them out of social jobs like warden, trader and negotiator. To see a particular ape's exact numbers, press the Summary button on their gene tab.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Apes are humanlike people with moods, so they make wishes, vote in elections and keep journals like everyone else.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Alpha Genes
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Over 300 new genes, new xenotypes, abandoned biotech labs and gene tools
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Strangers from the xenohuman union may carry xenotypes you designed yourself.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Alpha Genes adds a great many genes to Biotech, from small tweaks to very strong ones, and more than a dozen new xenotypes. Two new factions are built from xenotypes you design yourself. Abandoned biotech lab quests and genetic tools let you collect and change genes during play, which matters in a medieval game where gene machines are probably out of reach.

li.heading: Genes and strangers
li.text:
By the mod's own count there are more than 300 new genes, and a few extra ones appear with Alpha Animals and Alpha Biomes, both in your list. A "custom random" xenotype puts your own xenotype designs into two new factions: the civil xenohuman union and the xenohuman pirate gang.
Some xenotypes come with heavy drawbacks, so read a stranger's genes before you recruit them.

li.heading: Labs and gene tools
li.text: Abandoned biotech lab quests give access to the new genes. Gene tools come from lab quests and ordinary quest rewards: the gene remover takes out a random gene and the germline mutator adds a random one. Either puts the target in a coma for 3 days, so use them in a quiet season. If Rimedieval keeps your research medieval, treat found tools and recruits as your only way into genetics.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Genetics Expanded
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Hybrid animals from mixed genomes; in a medieval game, mostly a source of monsters
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: We can't build the genetics labs, but the hybrid monstrosities still find their way to us.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Vanilla Genetics Expanded lets a colony extract animal genomes and grow hybrid creatures in a genetics lab. All of its research is industrial or spacer tier, and Rimedieval limits your research to medieval, so you won't build the labs. What still reaches you are abandoned lab quests and the occasional pack of roaming monstrosities.

li.heading: Roaming monstrosities
li.text:
Roaming monstrosities are packs of hybrid manhunters, and their letter warns about greater scaria. Fight them from behind walls, like any manhunter pack. Alpha Animals, Dinosauria and Megafauna, all in your list, get full hybrid families.
The mod's quests and raids run on their own timer outside the storyteller, and the mod options set how often they come. If they come too often, lower the raid and quest frequency there rather than removing the mod.

li.heading: The labs
li.text: Its five genetics projects are industrial tier and mechahybridization is spacer tier. If you take an abandoned lab quest, expect genetics gear your medieval colony can't use itself.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A monstrosity that mauls a colonist and gets away can be given a name and come back as a nemesis.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Alpha Memes
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: New memes, structures, styles and rituals, including a whole set of funerals
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: We buried him in a pyramid, as our creed asks.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Alpha Memes adds new memes, ideoligion structures and a huge number of building and apparel styles, plus rituals such as sparring matches, rodeos, baptisms and many kinds of funeral.

table.li: Kind | Examples
Memes that reshape a colony | Deep devotion (live underground), pain is divine, naked truth
Combat memes | Gladiator (glory is won hand to hand and ranged weapons are shameful), sharpshooter, bulwark
Other memes | Monastic, artist, cowboys, water primacy, deforestation, gauranlen supremacy
Structures | Kemetic, Mesoamerican, Jewish, Jain and Sikh origins, neolithic, corsair, scavenger, atheism
Funerals | Cremation, mummification, sky burial, pyramid burial
Buildings | Pyramids, a sphinx, megaliths, a grand gate, a baptismal font, crude stone and wooden tables

li.heading: Choosing your memes
li.text: Memes are chosen when you found your ideoligion, and adding the mod to a running game changes nothing without dev mode, so decide your memes before you start. Think twice about gladiator if your defense relies on archers, since bows count as ranged weapons. Deep devotion suits a mountain colony, especially one with Stoneborn.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A funeral that cremates the body settles a colonist's wish for a proper burial, just as a grave would.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Memes and Structures
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Dozens of memes and structures, from aristocratic and republic to craft culture, with rituals to match
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: We built a wicker man from our own lumber and burned it for the ritual.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Memes and Structures adds a long list of memes and religious structures to pick when you found your ideoligion, many with their own rituals, buildings, roles and needs. Plenty suit a medieval realm: aristocratic, royal, republic, craft culture, city builders, bushido, fire worship, nomad and elders.

li.heading: Who rules
li.text:
The leadership memes are aristocratic, royal, god emperor, exalted priesthood, and republic, which adds a second and a third triumvir. For a feudal colony, aristocratic or royal plus craft culture or city builders fits the medieval mods in your list.
The elders meme asks the colony to respect and heed its old, and the mod also adds an elder trait.

li.heading: Rituals and other memes
li.text:
Rituals include the bonfire, wicker man burning, divine the stars, the trading fair, the leadership challenge, slave emancipation and incantation. A trading fair suits a merchant colony that sees many caravans.
Other memes include trader, party life, pacifist, vegan, healthcare, cultured, sweet teeth and fishing culture. Fire worship wants flames around, so in a wooden town keep the flames in stone rooms. The council's advisor already warns about wooden walls near open fires.

li.heading: Corruption in the eldritch cult
li.text: The eldritch cult structure adds a corruption need. It fades daily, obelisks pause it and incantations raise it. At 100 the pawn breaks; at 0 they are easily converted.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The council's offices sit beside your ideoligion's roles. Under an aristocratic, royal or god emperor creed the colony holds no council elections; its leader names the officers instead.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Splits and Schisms
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: A big colony can split into two rival ideoligions
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: After the schism, some of our people followed the new creed and the rest kept the old one.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Splits and Schisms adds the ideological schism: once your colony is big enough, part of it can break away into a new ideoligion that differs from yours by a meme or two. The two creeds then compete inside the colony until one of them is gone, and only then can another schism happen.

li.text:
The new ideoligion is close to the old one, with one or two different memes, and only part of the colony follows it, not everyone. It is meant as a threat for colonies that have grown large, so expect it as yours grows, and keep a moral guide able to convert: winning the breakaways back ends the split.
Extensive mod options make schisms rarer, gentler or harsher, so if they come too often for your taste, tune them there. The mod can be added to a running game.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Council votes follow skill, suitability and friendship, not creed, so a schism doesn't split the council on its own.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: ideoligion icons and relics
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: More ideoligion symbols, and dozens of new relics including helmets and armor
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Our relic is an old knight's helmet, chosen when the creed was founded.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Two small Vanilla Ideology Expanded modules that widen your choices when you design an ideoligion. Both take effect when an ideoligion is created, so they matter most at the start of a game. Both can be added mid-game, but they only affect ideoligions created afterward.

li.text:
Icons and Symbols adds over 200 new ideoligion icons, tagged so they only appear on fitting ideoligions.
Relics and Artifacts adds over 40 new relics, such as scrolls, statuettes, idols and sword shards. Apparel like helmets and armor can be chosen as a relic too, so a crown, helmet or blade shard makes a fitting relic for a medieval creed. The relic picker gets a search bar, which helps you find a particular item among the hundreds on offer.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Traits Expanded
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: More than 50 new traits, and a switch to stop any trait from appearing
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A drunken master hits harder with every drink in him.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Vanilla Traits Expanded adds dozens of traits: some bring new mechanics, some are quirky story traits and some are plain stat boosts. Its mod options can also switch off any trait, from the base game or another mod, so it stops appearing on new pawns.

li.heading: The new traits
li.text:
There are more than 50, such as drunken master, mad surgeon, heavy sleeper, kleptomaniac, perfectionist, snob, vengeful, wanderlust and workaholic. A drunken master hits harder the more alcohol is in them; a mad surgeon suffers no mood penalty from harvesting organs; a heavy sleeper can't have their sleep disturbed; and a perfectionist production specialist can make legendary items.
A few of the new ones, like kleptomaniac, are real burdens, so read each newcomer's traits.

li.heading: Switching traits off
li.text:
Switching a trait off sets its commonality to zero; pawns who already have it keep it. In a wooden medieval town, consider switching off pyromaniac.
Load the mod above any other trait mods, as its authors recommend. Trait and Backstory Icons and RimTraits Vanilla Trait Colors, both in your list, support all of its traits.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Many of these traits have opinions on decrees (workaholics love long hours, rebels hate being told what to do), count in council elections and bring wishes of their own, such as books for an academian or a caravan trip for the wanderlust-struck.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: RimTraits: General Traits and Trait Colors
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: 46 smaller attribute traits, and trait labels colored by how rare they are
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The rarer the trait, the stronger it tends to be.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: RimTraits - General Traits adds smaller traits that describe a pawn's body and mind, in tiers that get rarer as they get stronger. RimTraits - Vanilla Trait Colors recolors trait labels by how common they are, using the same scheme, for the base game and a few supported mods.

li.text:
General Traits has 46 traits. Some exclude each other, and the stronger tiers are rarer. Trait and Backstory Icons has icons for all 46.
Vanilla Trait Colors recolors the base game's traits and those of General Traits, Vanilla Traits Expanded, Vanilla Fishing Expanded and Medieval Overhaul. Read the color as rarity, not as good or bad. Keep it next to Trait and Backstory Icons: for traits without their own icon, the icon mod picks one from these colors.
The same author makes RimTraits - Medieval Talents, also in your list.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: These don't change council reactions yet; the council reads the base game's traits and those of Vanilla Traits Expanded.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: People Can Change
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Colonists slowly gain, lose or shift traits as the years go by
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: After a long stretch of good moods, she turned optimist.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: People Can Change lets colonists change over time: they can gain a trait, lose one, or move up or down a trait's scale. Some changes follow from what they live through, such as long happiness or misery, eating human meat or getting used to a new body.

li.heading: What changes people

table.li: What they live through | Chance | What changes
Staying happy, or staying close to breaking | Roughly 1 in 2 at each check, about once a quadrum | They turn optimist or depressive (this can be switched off)
Eating human meat | 1 in 100 cooked, 1 in 300 raw | They become a cannibal
Being a body purist | 1 in 3 each quadrum | They let it go, and 1 in 3 of those turn transhumanist

li.after: In a famine, think twice before serving human meat: it can make a cannibal for life.

li.heading: Limits and settings
li.text:
New traits stop at a maximum, 4 by default, and a minimum can be set as well. It works with modded traits, and the settings choose which traits can be gained or lost, so block the ones you never want gained, such as pyromaniac. It can be added to or removed from a save.
Vanilla Social Interactions Expanded can also give out traits. If traits change too often, turn off one of the two.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The council reads traits as they are now, so a colonist who turns kind, greedy or industrious reacts to decrees, dilemmas and secrets accordingly from then on.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Skills Expanded and Alpha Skills
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Permanent expertise, and new passions like natural, critical, apathy and many conditional ones
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A critical passion for cooking makes a fast-learning cook and a slow learner at everything else.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Vanilla Skills Expanded lets a colonist with a passion and a high skill pick one permanent expertise, a specialty within that skill. It also adds three passions: apathy, natural and critical. Alpha Skills builds on it with dozens more passions, many of which switch on only under certain conditions, and more expertises.

li.heading: How fast each passion learns

table.li: Passion | Learning speed
None | 35%
Interested | 100%
Burning | 150%
Apathy | 25%
Natural | 200%
Critical | 300%

li.after: Natural passions also forget three times as fast, so keep natural-passion colonists working at their skill, or they lose it fast. Critical passions never forget, but by default they slow every other skill to a quarter.

li.heading: Expertise
li.text: Expertise is one per colonist and permanent. The mod says it needs a passion and a skill above 15, and only your own colonists get it. Examples include weaponsmithing, tailoring, surgery, first aid, dueling, hunting, architecture and smoothing. Since it can't be undone, choose carefully, and pick what the colony lacks, such as weaponsmithing or surgery.

li.heading: Alpha Skills
li.text: Alpha Skills adds 26 passions and 19 expertises. Passions like drunken, night, rainy day, vengeful, nomadic and competitive learn much faster only while their condition holds, so match them to the work: put colonists with the night passion on night shifts, and those with the rainy day passion outdoors when it rains.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Passions are judged by how fast they make someone learn. Apathy counts as no passion, natural and critical count as burning, and an Alpha Skills passion that switches on and off counts by its current state. A colonist close to unlocking an expertise in a skill they love may set their heart on earning one.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Social Interactions Expanded
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Richer free time: best friends, venting, teaching, dates, gatherings and aspirations
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: After supper, a few of them went out together to look at the stars.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Vanilla Social Interactions Expanded changes what colonists do in their spare time. They make best friends, vent to friends, teach each other, go on dates, and gather for meals, walks, drinks and parties. Aspirations give colonists short goals to chase, and inspirations are reworked. Every mechanic can be switched off in the mod options.

li.heading: Gatherings
li.text: Group activities include a meal together, a walk, grabbing a beer, skygazing, viewing art, building snowmen, parties, birthday parties and funerals. Give them a place to happen: a proper dining room and a rec area. Movie night needs a television, so it won't come up in a medieval colony.

li.heading: Friends, traits and inspirations
li.text:
Its mechanics cover memories, inspiration changes, gaining new traits, venting, friends and best friends, teaching, discord, group activities, dating and more. Best friends get their own grief when one dies, is sold or is killed. The new inspirations are planting, mining, cooking, research, learning, party, flirting and melee frenzy.
Since it can also hand out traits, like People Can Change, switch one of the two off if traits change too often.

points.li: Its lessons, venting, memories and best friends feed the council's bonds, and lessons that keep coming can grow into a mentorship.
Its aspirations are short inspiration tasks, not life goals.
When a granted wish turns into an inspiration that doesn't match the wish, it can be one of these new ones.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Go-juice
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: A druid's Gaulish potion: go-juice for colonies with no drug lab
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Our druid brews the potion over the fire, and only she knows the rest of the recipe.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Medieval Go-juice adds a Gaulish potion brewed by druids, so medieval and tribal colonies, and their go-juice-hungry Hussars, aren't left without it. It needs no research, but it needs a rare brewer: a good cook who is also a scholar. The mod also adds a weak psychite joint that needs no research.

li.heading: Brewing the potion

table.li: Brewing | Details
Station | A fueled cooking station, or Medieval Overhaul's stew pot
Brewer | Cooking 10 and Intellectual 10
Ingredients | Psychoid leaves; the rest is a druid's secret
Research | None
Shelf life | About 7 days since a 2025 update, which also made it quicker to make

li.after: Find your druid early by looking for a colonist with both Cooking and Intellectual at 10 or more, and keep a stock of psychoid leaves, from your own field or from traders.

li.heading: Before a fight
li.text: The potion doesn't keep for long, so brew a batch when a raid looks likely rather than stockpiling it. Treat it like any go-juice: dose your fighters, not your whole colony.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: trait, gene and level-up helpers
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Small helpers that make traits, xenotypes and skill gains easier to read
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: With the trait icons, you can read a newcomer's bio tab at a glance.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Four small interface mods in your list. None of them change the game's balance; they make it easier to see who your people are and what they can do.

li.heading: The four helpers

table.li: Mod | What it shows you
Level Up! | A notice whenever a colonist gains a skill level, with a cooldown so skill decay doesn't flood you with messages
Trait and Backstory Icons | Icons next to traits and backstories in the bio tab, with icons for Vanilla Traits Expanded, RimTraits, Medieval Overhaul, Alpha Memes, Alpha Genes and A RimWorld of Magic
Xenotype Summary | A Summary button on the gene tab, info cards, the xenotype creator and the gene assembler that lists every gene's effect and adds up the totals
Vanilla Races Expanded - Custom Icons | Hundreds of extra icons for xenotypes you design in the xenotype creator

li.after:
Before you recruit an elf, stoneborn, merren or ape, open their info card and press Summary.
A skill bouncing between levels 9 and 10, or 19 and 20, is the base game's skill decay, not a bug. If the level-up notices get too chatty, tune them in Level Up's mod settings.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: hair and menu looks
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: New hairstyles and a barber's table, sharper vanilla hair, and new menu backgrounds
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The barber's table can trim a beard, change a hairstyle or dye hair a new color.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Three cosmetic mods in your list. They change how your people and the game's menus look, not how the game plays.

li.heading: The barber's table
li.text:
Vanilla Hair Expanded adds about a hundred new hairstyles in the base game's style, and a barber's table in the Misc tab to change hair, hair color and beard. The table costs 75 wood or metal plus 20 steel: build it from wood to save metal, but have its 20 steel ready. It is also a quick way to tell lookalike colonists apart at a glance.
The mod can be added or removed mid-game, and its barber's table finds hairstyles from every hair mod.

li.heading: Sharper hair and new menus
li.text: Vanilla Hair Retextured gives every base game and DLC hairstyle sharper, more consistent textures. Vanilla Backgrounds Expanded adds new main menu and loading screen backgrounds, which you can pick and cycle in the mod options. It adds menu art, not pawn backstories.
